title: Spinach, frozen, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Spinach is a leafy vegetable rich in vitamins and minerals. Frozen cooked spinach with no added fat retains most of its nutrients and is convenient for quick preparation.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Spinach belongs to the Amaranthaceae family and grows in temperate climates.
Freezing preserves up to 90 % of vitamin C and almost all folate.
Spinach contains plant sterols – carotenoids that become more bioavailable after heating.
In many cuisines spinach is used in pies, quiches, and stuffed dumplings.
Cooked spinach has lower oxalate levels than raw, making it safer for people prone to kidney stones.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Iron from spinach supports hemoglobin levels, especially when paired with vitamin C.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin protect the eyes from age‑related degeneration.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: One cup of cooked spinach provides fewer than 40 calories, helpful for weight management.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber promotes regular bowel movements and supports gut microbiota.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: High oxalate content may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, people may experience an allergic reaction to spinach.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If salt is added during processing, sodium levels can rise; choose the unsalted version when possible.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Frozen cooked spinach can be heated in the microwave or sautéed, added to soups, stews, omelets, pasta, or blended into a smooth puree.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in the freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. After thawing, use within 2–3 days and do not refreeze.
